analysis.title: Election 2026: What The Results Mean For Financials, Housing & Crypto
key_insights: Democrats were projected as of Tuesday night to win both the Senate and the House. TD Cowen views this as negative for financials, housing and crypto, but says it will not stop regulators from pursuing de-regulatory agendas over the next two years.
Items to watch: the lame duck session, congressional investigations of Trump, the debt ceiling and populist legislation such as interest rate caps.
Debt ceiling: there will be a push to raise it in the lame duck, but TD Cowen is dubious it succeeds because Democrats will want to use the vote next year to force policy concessions from Trump.

De-regulation: bank regulators will advance rules on capital, liquidity and tiering despite the election. The SEC and CFTC should stay active on crypto, prediction markets and perps, and no changes at these agencies are expected.

Clarity Act: Sherrod Brown winning in Ohio damages the crypto industry's political clout, since the industry worked to defeat him. TD Cowen did not think Clarity could advance over the next two years and is now more confident in that view.

Democrats will investigate Trump's crypto entanglements, including World Liberty Financial. TD Cowen says the resulting political environment may make it impossible to pass a version of Clarity the crypto sector could back.

Interest rate caps: Trump and Sen. Elizabeth Warren agree on capping rates. TD Cowen sees this as a risk, but expects a cap closer to 36% than the 10% Trump has sought, so it may affect fintechs more than banks.

Bill Pulte is expected to remain FHFA director even if he takes other White House jobs. This means continued risk to FICO, mortgage insurers and title insurers, and the expedited refinancing plan should advance even if it hurts MBS investors.
Housing: Rep. Maxine Waters will focus on down payment help and funds to renovate public housing. TD Cowen is dubious it becomes law.

Consumer protection: Elizabeth Warren is expected to be the next Senate Banking chair, which means a focus on the CFPB and consumer protections and possible headline risk to consumer finance companies.
M&A: no impact expected on bank merger approvals despite Democratic control of Congress.
Confirmations: Democrats are not expected to confirm Trump nominees unless Trump fills Democratic seats at agencies like the FDIC and SEC, which he is unlikely to do.
Fed Governor Lisa Cook: the inability to confirm a replacement may make Trump less inclined to fire Cook.

sector_views.rationale: Democratic control of Congress is viewed as negative, with rate cap and consumer protection headline risk, though bank deregulation by regulators continues.
Continued FHFA risk under Pulte for FICO, mortgage insurers and title insurers. Housing bills from Waters are unlikely to become law.
Brown's win and Trump investigations weaken the industry's political clout and make a Clarity Act version the sector could back unlikely.

crypto_views: TD Cowen sees the Clarity Act as unable to advance over the next two years, with Sherrod Brown's Ohio win reducing the crypto industry's political clout.
Democrats are expected to investigate Trump's crypto entanglements including World Liberty Financial, which may make a Clarity version the industry could back impossible.
The SEC and CFTC are expected to remain active on crypto, prediction markets and perps, with no personnel changes at those agencies.
risk_factors: Populist interest rate cap legislation backed by both Trump and Sen. Warren, likely nearer 36% than 10%, with more impact on fintechs than banks.
Continued FHFA risk under Bill Pulte for FICO, mortgage insurers and title insurers.
Headline risk to consumer finance companies from Warren's expected Senate Banking chairmanship and CFPB focus.
Failure to raise the debt ceiling in the lame duck as Democrats seek leverage.
Congressional investigations of Trump, including crypto entanglements.
